Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $40 million class fund with automatic payments to all identified members, plus $10 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline would not oppose that fee request, and any amount the court declines to award would be added to the class fund rather than revert to Brightline. Automatic distribution is essential given Brightline’s ability to identify and pay the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is willing to pursue a court-approvable settlement with automatic payments, but cannot accept a $50 million total outlay. We propose a $25 million class fund and $5 million in fees and expenses, with fees subject to court approval, no clear-sailing commitment, and any unawarded fees reverting to Brightline.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s willingness to use automatic payments and to state fees separately. We can move from our opening position, but the class fund must provide materially greater relief, and any fee the court does not award should benefit the class rather than Brightline. Our revised package is set out below; the fee remains subject to court approval, and Brightline need not agree not to oppose it.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline recognizes the importance of meaningful, automatic payments and is prepared to improve its offer substantially. We can propose a $32 million class fund and $7 million in fees and expenses, with no clear-sailing commitment and any unawarded fees added to the class fund. This is a $39 million total package, with fees subject to court approval. We cannot accept a package exceeding Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s movement on automatic distribution and on directing any court-declined fee amount to the class. To resolve this within Brightline’s stated $40 million all-in authority, we propose a $33 million class fund and $7 million in fees and expenses, with automatic payments, no clear-sailing commitment, and any unawarded fee added to the class fund. Fees remain subject to court approval.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts Hargrove Lane LLP’s latest term sheet, subject to court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Preserve confidential valuation and litigation assessment. Use the channel to establish constructive tone and emphasize a meaningful, automatically distributed class benefit without anchoring.

Preserve Brightline’s settlement authority while encouraging class counsel to make the first concrete proposal. Signal willingness to consider automatic payments, without committing to a fund or fee amount.

Open with a strong but supportable demand that reflects the substantial disputed charges and the value of certain, automatic recovery. Keep fees separate and protect the class if the court reduces them. This is a proposal, not an acceptance.

The opening demand exceeds Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority. Counter well below the cap while preserving automatic payments and court review of fees; require any unawarded fee amount to return to Brightline and do not provide clear sailing.

Preserve negotiating leverage by not disclosing the firm’s confidential valuation or making an off-record monetary commitment. Emphasize automatic payments and separate, court-approved fees, and reserve a complete proposal for the formal exchange.
Acknowledge the importance of automatic payments without revealing Brightline’s ceiling or making a commitment. Request their complete proposal so the formal exchange can be focused.

The defense’s $25 million fund and $5 million fee offer is too low, particularly because it sends any court-rejected fee back to Brightline. Make a substantial but more movement-signaling counter that preserves automatic payments and directs any unawarded fee to the class. Keep the fee separate and subject to court approval; omit clear sailing to address a likely defense concern. Do not accept the latest offer.

Hargrove Lane’s latest proposal exceeds Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority. Make a serious counter within the cap, retaining automatic distribution and their preferred treatment of unawarded fees while keeping fees subject to court approval and rejecting clear sailing. A $32 million fund plus $7 million fees totals $39 million.

I should not disclose our confidential merits assessment, reservation value, or fee economics. The prior exchanges already establish the importance of automatic payments and separately stated fees, so this message should probe defense flexibility on the most important structural terms without making a premature monetary offer.

Signal willingness on automatic distribution and a class-benefiting disposition of any declined fee amount, while making clear that any agreement depends on the complete package and court approval. Do not disclose settlement authority or commit to specific economics before the formal exchange.

Brightline’s latest offer is $39 million all-in, and its stated authority caps total outlay at $40 million. A $33 million class fund with the same $7 million fee reaches that cap and directs the incremental value to class members. Preserve automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and transfer of any unawarded fee to the class. Do not accept the latest offer yet.

The latest term sheet totals Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority, preserves automatic distribution, has no clear-sailing commitment, and directs any unawarded fee amount to the class without increasing the total outlay. Accepting secures a court-approvable resolution within the authorized cap.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement was reached through arm’s-length negotiations between experienced counsel, informed by the strengths and risks of the claims and defenses, the risks of class certification and trial, and the time and expense of continued litigation. Consistent with the confidentiality of the mediation communications, this statement does not recount confidential negotiating positions or offers. The agreement provides a $33 million class fund, automatic distribution to identified class members, and attorneys’ fees and expenses subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to a clear-sailing provision, and any fee amount not awarded by the Court will be added to the class fund.

backchannel.speaker: plaintiff
backchannel.message: We are prepared to explore a practical resolution, particularly one that delivers direct, automatic payments to identified members. We would welcome your view of Brightline’s settlement authority and the terms it is prepared to discuss. Any resolution would need to provide meaningful class relief, with fees addressed separately and subject to court approval.

backchannel.speaker: defense
backchannel.message: Brightline is prepared to discuss a court-approvable resolution, including direct automatic payments if the economics are workable. We are not setting a number off the record; please share the complete terms your client would propose, including the class fund, fees, and distribution method.

backchannel.speaker: plaintiff
backchannel.message: We will provide a complete term sheet in the formal exchange. Because Brightline can identify the members and payment cards, automatic distribution is central to a meaningful resolution; a claims process would needlessly reduce relief. Any fee request should be separate from the class fund and remain subject to court approval. Please come prepared to discuss a substantial fund on that basis.

backchannel.speaker: defense
backchannel.message: We understand that direct automatic payments are important where members are identifiable, and we are prepared to evaluate that approach alongside a separately stated fee request subject to court approval. Please include your proposed class-fund amount, fee amount, and requested fee-related terms in the formal exchange so we can assess a complete, court-approvable package.

backchannel.speaker: plaintiff
backchannel.message: We will submit a complete package in the formal exchange. To make that exchange productive, please let us know whether Brightline has authority to consider automatic payments with no claims process, and whether it can agree that any court-declined portion of the fee request would go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. We remain open to a practical resolution, but the class relief must be meaningful.

backchannel.speaker: defense
backchannel.message: Brightline has authority to consider automatic payments without a claims process, subject to agreement on the overall economics and a court-approvable package. We are also willing to discuss having any portion of an agreed fee amount that the court declines go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. That would remain subject to the complete term sheet and court approval; please include your proposed amounts and terms in the formal exchange.
